Complete project discussion and final setup

This is a consolidated, reorganized record of the discussion, not a verbatim chat export. It covers the original requirements, later changes, wiring, power questions, code, test findings and outstanding issues. Full saved project notes, all current firmware source, test scripts and available logs follow in appendices. Images are embedded: this HTML document is a single self-contained offline file.

Snapshot: 26 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata. Nothing was reflashed or operated to create this package. Current status below takes precedence over historical notes and the original wiring diagram.

Current status — read first

• Main board firmware was compiled, flashed and verified on an ESP32-D0WD-V3, MAC d4:8a:fc:61:62:f8.
• Glove board firmware was compiled, flashed and verified on another ESP32-D0WD-V3, MAC 20:9b:a9:99:28:5c. Its observed BLE address is 20:9b:a9:99:28:5e.
• The glove sensor now works. At I2C address 0x68, it returned WHO_AM_I=0x70, consistent with MPU6500 rather than MPU6050. A separate MPU6500 initialization/read path was added.
• Glove startup calibrated from 100 samples. Changing angle packets were observed and BLE CONNECTED was reported when the main board was powered.
• A movement check recorded 30 samples: roll −1.8° to 59.1°, pitch −13° to 18.7°, pan commands 88–149°, tilt commands 77–109°. These confirm sensor movement detection, not motor movement.
• Wheel diagnostics confirmed expected ESP32 direction/PWM readbacks for each side forward/reverse and return to zero. The user repeatedly reported NO PHYSICAL WHEEL MOVEMENT. Motor power/wiring/driver operation remain unresolved.
• OLED acknowledged at 0x3C. Servo signals were configured at 50Hz. Test text, colors, beep and servo commands were issued; visible movement/light/sound was not confirmed by the user.
• Ultrasonic readings were intermittent. PIR detection was not fully verified after its warmup. Laser remained off during diagnostics.
• A later main-only check reported link=0. Both boards must be powered nearby; an earlier connection does not guarantee the glove is currently connected.
• The last wheel test ended with all direction outputs and both enable duties at zero, wheels disarmed, stop and laser-off sent. Subsequent resets/commands may change the state.

Project and hardware roles

There are two ESP32s. The main ESP32 controls the chassis L298N, turret servos and turret peripherals. The glove ESP32 reads its own IMU and provides angle packets over BLE; the IMU is not physically wired to the main board.

Four DC motors move the chassis. MG995 pans the turret left/right; SG90 tilts it up/down. The payload can be the laser and/or ultrasonic sensor. PIR and ultrasonic data trigger indicators; they do not autonomously aim the turret or activate the laser.

Original diagram inventory: ESP32 ×2, MG995, SG90, MPU6050-described sensor, HC-SR04, PIR, laser, buzzer, OLED, RGB modules ×2, four 18650 cells and holder, perfboard, breadboards, jumper wires, external two-cell charger. Only one RGB module has a pin assignment. The sensor was subsequently identified as MPU6500-compatible.

Originally the four-wheel chassis was excluded and the motor driver listed as missing; the scope later expanded to include wheel control, and the chassis photo showed an L298N-style module. The receipts themselves were not examined here. The missing items noted in the original diagram included a battery regulator, glove portable-power/charging path, ultrasonic divider resistors and physical mode button. Not all gaps were resolved.

Main ESP32 wiring — matches the final firmware

Device / signal                   Main ESP32 / supply
MG995 pan signal                  GPIO13
SG90 tilt signal                  GPIO27
HC-SR04 TRIG                      GPIO5
HC-SR04 ECHO                      GPIO18 through divider below
PIR OUT                           GPIO19
OLED SDA / SCL                    GPIO21 / GPIO22
RGB R / G / B                     GPIO32 / GPIO33 / GPIO4
Laser logic/driver input          GPIO23
Buzzer transistor-driver input    GPIO25
L298N IN1 / IN2                   GPIO14 / GPIO16
L298N IN3 / IN4                   GPIO17 / GPIO26
L298N ENA / ENB                   GPIO2 / GPIO15
All signal grounds                Common GND

OLED supply: 3.3V, expected SSD1306 128×64 at 0x3C.
HC-SR04 and PIR supply: appropriate 5V.
Both servo V+: suitable EXTERNAL REGULATED 5V, sized for combined peak/stall current.
Laser supply: according to actual module rating; not established in this chat.
RGB: assumes suitable resistors/module inputs and common-cathode wiring by default.

This mapping targets the detected original ESP32, not arbitrary C3/S3 boards. GPIO16/17 may be unavailable on PSRAM boards. GPIO2 and GPIO15 are boot-strapping pins. GPIO2 must be low or floating at reset to enter serial download mode.

Glove wiring

Sensor VCC → glove ESP32 3V3
Sensor GND → glove ESP32 GND
Sensor SDA → GPIO21
Sensor SCL → GPIO22
AD0 → GND for I2C address 0x68
INT → unconnected

Firmware tries addresses 0x68 and 0x69. Address and identity differ: a device at address 0x68 is not necessarily an MPU6050. The current code supports MPU6050 plus the observed MPU6500-compatible identity 0x70. On initialization failure, it scans the I2C bus, reports addresses/chip identity and retries every three seconds.

Hold the glove flat and still for roughly one second at boot. Calibration averages 100 samples. Send lowercase c to the GLOVE serial port at 115200 baud to recalibrate. Calibration briefly pauses angle updates.

Angles use accelerometer-derived gravity orientation with smoothing. Gyro data is read by the driver, but gyro fusion, compass heading, yaw tracking and classified gesture commands are not implemented. Roll controls pan/steering; pitch controls tilt/throttle.

Four motors to L298N

Connect each side in parallel, only if the driver can handle that side's combined stall current.

OUT1 ──┬── Left-front motor wire A
       └── Left-rear motor wire A
OUT2 ──┬── Left-front motor wire B
       └── Left-rear motor wire B

OUT3 ──┬── Right-front motor wire A
       └── Right-rear motor wire A
OUT4 ──┬── Right-front motor wire B
       └── Right-rear motor wire B

Motor battery + → L298N VS / motor-power input
Motor battery − → L298N GND → ESP32 GND

Mirrored mounting can require opposite motor wire polarity. If one motor runs opposite to its partner, power off and swap only that motor's wires. If the entire side is reversed, swap both motors on that side or use INVERT_LEFT/INVERT_RIGHT in WheelDrive.h.

Clamp wires inside the screw terminals. A wire passing across a terminal block is not connected. Solder/secure motor-tab connections and insulate exposed joints from metal brackets. Motor power goes through suitable direct wiring and terminals, not breadboard rails.

Remove ENA and ENB enable jumper caps for ESP32 PWM. Connect ENA→GPIO2, ENB→GPIO15. Add 10kΩ pull-down from each enable to ground. The module's 5V REGULATOR jumper is separate and must be configured according to that exact module and supply voltage. Do not connect a module's 5V jumper pin to an ESP32 GPIO.

Power: USB, batteries, 3V3 and the missing regulator

YES: the ESP32 can run from USB while batteries power the motor controller. Share grounds.

USB computer / USB power bank → ESP32 USB
Suitable motor battery +      → L298N VS / motor-power input
Motor battery negative        → L298N GND → ESP32 GND
ESP32 GPIOs                   → L298N control inputs

USB powering the ESP32 does not supply the motors.
The L298N also needs its proper logic supply; its onboard regulator/jumper configuration was not established in this chat.
A lit controller LED does not prove adequate motor power.

Do NOT power motors from ESP32 3V3.
Do NOT connect raw battery-pack voltage to ESP32 3V3.
Do NOT connect controller 5V to ESP32 3V3.
While USB powers the ESP32, keep controller 5V disconnected from ESP32 VIN/5V unless the exact board's power circuitry provides appropriate isolation.
Do not assume a four-cell holder's topology or voltage; measure it and use suitable battery protection/charging.

Without an external regulator, retain USB or a USB power bank for the ESP32. This does not solve the servos' separate regulated high-current supply requirement. Do not power MG995/SG90 through ESP32 3V3 or its board regulator.

Future battery operation:
Battery → motor driver supply, if suitable for the motors
Battery → appropriate regulated 5V → ESP32 VIN/5V, if that board accepts it
Suitable regulated servo supply → servo V+
All negatives → common ground
Disconnect USB before using an external 5V feed unless properly isolated.

The external two-cell charger is not an inline regulator. It does not establish a suitable charging path for an assembled four-cell pack. A portable glove battery/charger/boost path was discussed but not built or verified.

Disconnect USB and batteries before rewiring. Use breadboards for suitable low-current electronics/signals; bypass their rails for motor and servo current.

HC-SR04 divider, RGB, buzzer, OLED and laser

ECHO ── 1kΩ ──┬── GPIO18
              └── 2kΩ ── GND

Never connect 5V ECHO directly to GPIO18. No echo means unknown range, not clear space.

Example active buzzer NPN driver:
GPIO25 → 1kΩ → base
base → 10kΩ → GND
emitter → GND
collector → buzzer negative
buzzer positive → suitable 5V
For an inductive magnetic buzzer, use an appropriate flyback diode.
Default code assumes active buzzer; PASSIVE_BUZZER changes tone behavior.

RGB assumes current limiting and compatible inputs. Bare LEDs need individual resistors. Common-anode or incompatible 5V modules need matching wiring/settings/drivers. The second RGB module has no independent GPIO/code assignment.

OLED assumption: SSD1306, 128×64, address0x3C. Different address/resolution or SH1106 controller needs changes. ACK confirms a bus response, not visible pixels.

PIR is ignored during the first ~60 seconds after reset. Motion or ultrasonic distance below30cm triggers red indication and short periodic beeps. These readings are advisory, not wheel collision avoidance.

Three-pin laser: GPIO23 may drive S only if compatible with 3.3V logic. VCC must match the actual module rating; GND is common.
Two-wire laser: use a suitable transistor/MOSFET driver; do not power it from GPIO23.
Use appropriate input pull-down so the laser stays off during boot. Its actual voltage/current/optical power were not established. Use a low-power visible indicator and keep its beam away from eyes and reflective surfaces.

Laser mounting for both servo axes

Chassis
└── MG995 pan servo fixed upright
    └── Pan bracket attached to MG995 horn
        └── SG90 tilt servo mounted sideways
            └── Tilt cradle attached to SG90 horn
                └── Laser secured to cradle

The laser is mechanically carried by nested brackets, not electrically connected to both servo signals. MG995 rotates the entire upper assembly; SG90 tilts the laser cradle. Keep it lightweight and support the load rather than bending the small servo shaft.

Command servos to90° before fitting horns, then align the laser straight ahead. Leave flexible wire slack and keep it clear of gears. Current pan limit:30–150°. Tilt:45–135°. Servo pulse range:1000–2000µs. Reduce travel if the mechanism binds. These are not continuous-rotation axes.

Keep the laser disconnected during mechanical adjustment. A suitable external regulated servo supply is still needed.

Main-board commands — 115200 baud, case sensitive

g       Turret gesture mode; wheels disabled/disarmed
d       Wheel gesture mode; freeze turret; neutral glove for0.5s to arm
s / h   Stop/disarm wheels; hold turret; laser off; abort peripheral test
c       Stop wheels and center turret at90°, remain in hold
l       Lowercase L: manual1s laser pulse, fresh link and turret gesture mode only
0       Zero: laser off
i       I2C scan; servo attachment/frequency; wheel duty; PIR raw/warmup
p       Wheel direction GPIO and enable-duty readbacks
t       RGB/OLED/buzzer/small servo-sweep test; wheels and laser off
u / v   Left / right forward:200ms at duty80/255
U / V   Left / right forward:1500ms at duty180/255
J / K   Left / right reverse:1500ms at duty180/255

GLOVE command:
c       Recalibrate neutral while still

The same lowercase c means different things on the two boards. Identify which ESP32 is attached. Both boards used /dev/cu.usbserial-0001 at different times; the serial-port name is not a board identity.

Main startup defaults to turret gesture behavior with wheels disabled. Stop/hold persists until another mode command or reset. In wheel mode, pitch drives forward/reverse; roll steers; roll at neutral pitch turns in place. Neutral stops the wheels. Normal drive is capped at120/255, distinct from the explicit180/255 extended diagnostics.

Mode switching currently requires main-board USB serial. No physical mode button or glove mode-switch gesture is implemented.

BLE behavior, timeouts and limitations

Glove server name: GestureGlove. Main BLE client name: GestureTurret.
Shared service UUID: 60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000001
Read characteristic: 60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000002
ASCII packet: sequence,pan,tilt

Glove updates about every40ms; main reads about every50ms. Main freshness threshold is300ms. Stale data/link loss holds turret position and disables the laser in main-loop logic.

A separate FreeRTOS wheel task rejects main-loop command-update gaps over250ms and disarms the wheels. Neutral rearming is required after loss. End-to-end latency also includes packet freshness and scheduling; this is not a certified hard real-time system.
Direction reversal includes at least150ms bridge-off time.
Explicit wheel diagnostics bypass glove arming but have task-enforced duration caps up to1500ms and duty180.
Disabling outputs coasts motors; it is not a mechanical brake.

BLE scans/reads are synchronous and may delay display, sensors and serial-command processing. Wheel pulse expiry runs independently. BLE is an unauthenticated demonstration without pairing/whitelisting. No physical emergency stop, collision avoidance, autonomous targeting or laser activation was implemented.

Test and troubleshooting history

1. Initial sandbox restrictions blocked downloads and USB. Later access changes allowed library installation and flashing.
2. Main firmware compiled and flashed. Wheel functionality and diagnostics were added later.
3. With the controller connected, uploads repeatedly failed with boot mode0xB. Disconnecting GPIO2→ENA allowed uploads. Correct the enable/jumper/pull-down wiring rather than endlessly retrying the same boot-strapping condition.
4. A USB connection sometimes failed with termios Invalid argument in both Python and Arduino tools. Unplugging/reconnecting restored communication. Failed-open attempts sent no wheel commands.
5. A first extended-test runner sampled before the motor task had applied a queued command and measured expiry from send time despite BLE delays. It was corrected to synchronize to the ESP32 acknowledgement and poll through the pulse.
6. Repeated200ms/duty80 and1500ms/duty180 tests passed ESP32 GPIO/PWM checks and returned to zero. User observed no movement. Physical wheel operation remains unresolved.
7. The chassis photo appeared to show an empty front motor-output terminal, exposed motor wiring and possibly an empty battery-holder slot. These were tentative image observations; no definitive wiring fault was established from that photo.
8. Glove initially found no I2C devices. After wiring changes,0x68 responded but WHO_AM_I0x70 was rejected by the MPU6050-only driver.
9. MPU6500 support was added, flashed at115200 and hash-verified.100-sample calibration succeeded and angle packets changed.
10. Glove reported CONNECTED with main powered. A live movement check confirmed significant roll/pitch changes.

Why none of the motors may move

Check shared causes first: no motor supply; battery voltage collapsing under load; missing controller logic supply; missing common ground; ENA/ENB disabled or miswired; mistaken physical pins; loose breadboard/screw-terminal connections; motors not connected to outputs; wrong controller model; overloaded/damaged driver; insufficient motor-terminal voltage due to driver loss; motor fault or mechanical jam.

The L298N must support two motors' combined stall current per side. USB alone does not power the motor rail. A controller LED alone is insufficient evidence.

Useful next evidence: clear top-down controller photograph showing labels and jumpers, battery topology/rating, measured voltage at VS-to-GND and under load. Check actual driver input and output voltages when appropriate. Never put a meter in current mode directly across a supply. Power off before changing wires. Test a disconnected motor only with a supply matching its rating.

Compile and flash from the extracted ZIP

In Arduino IDE, install dependencies, select the correct board/port, open the intended sketch, Verify and Upload. Glove flashing at921600 once lost verification;115200 succeeded.

CLI from package root:
arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 --output-dir build/turret turret
arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 --output-dir build/glove glove

Replace PORT with the intended board's serial port:
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32:UploadSpeed=115200 --port PORT --input-dir build/turret turret
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32:UploadSpeed=115200 --port PORT --input-dir build/glove glove

Alternative full merged-image flash, after installing esptool:
python -m esptool --chip esp32 --port PORT --baud 115200 write-flash 0x0 build/turret/turret.ino.merged.bin
python -m esptool --chip esp32 --port PORT --baud 115200 write-flash 0x0 build/glove/glove.ino.merged.bin

The plain .ino.bin is the application image, not the full image. Do not write it at offset0. Merged images include bootloader and partitions. MANIFEST_SHA256.json contains archive-file checksums. *_flashed.bin files are retained uploader artifacts; use named merged images or rebuild.

Before main flashing, turn motor power off and release the GPIO2 strap if needed. Never select the glove build for the main board just because the port name matches.

Complete current firmware source

glove/Mpu6500.h
#pragma once
#include <Wire.h>
#include <Adafruit_Sensor.h>

// MPU6500: WHO_AM_I=0x70. Separate initialization from the MPU6050 driver.
class Mpu6500 {
 public:
  bool begin(uint8_t address) {
    address_=address;
    uint8_t id;
    if (!read(0x75,&id,1) || id!=0x70) return false;
    if (!write(0x6B,0x80)) return false; // device reset
    delay(100);
    if (!write(0x6B,0x01)) return false; // wake, automatic PLL clock
    delay(100);
    if (!write(0x6C,0x00) || !write(0x1A,0x04) || // all axes, gyro DLPF 20Hz
        !write(0x19,0x09) || !write(0x1B,0x00) || // 100Hz, +/-250 deg/s
        !write(0x1C,0x08) || !write(0x1D,0x04)) return false; // +/-4g, accel DLPF
    uint8_t range;
    return read(0x1C,&range,1) && (range&0x18)==0x08;
  }

  bool getEvent(sensors_event_t *a,sensors_event_t *g,sensors_event_t *t) {
    uint8_t data[14];
    if (!read(0x3B,data,sizeof(data))) return false;
    *a={}; *g={}; *t={};
    a->acceleration.x=word(data)*9.80665f/8192;
    a->acceleration.y=word(data+2)*9.80665f/8192;
    a->acceleration.z=word(data+4)*9.80665f/8192;
    t->temperature=word(data+6)/333.87f+21.0f;
    constexpr float gyroScale=0.01745329252f/131;
    g->gyro.x=word(data+8)*gyroScale;
    g->gyro.y=word(data+10)*gyroScale;
    g->gyro.z=word(data+12)*gyroScale;
    // All-zero acceleration is not a usable gravity orientation sample.
    return a->acceleration.x!=0 || a->acceleration.y!=0 || a->acceleration.z!=0;
  }

 private:
  uint8_t address_=0x68;
  static int16_t word(const uint8_t *p) { return (int16_t)((uint16_t)p[0]<<8 | p[1]); }
  bool write(uint8_t reg,uint8_t value) {
    Wire.beginTransmission(address_); Wire.write(reg); Wire.write(value);
    return Wire.endTransmission()==0;
  }
  bool read(uint8_t reg,uint8_t *buffer,uint8_t length) {
    Wire.beginTransmission(address_); Wire.write(reg);
    if (Wire.endTransmission(false)!=0) return false;
    if (Wire.requestFrom(address_,length)!=length) return false;
    for (int i=0;i<length;++i) buffer[i]=Wire.read();
    return true;
  }
};
glove/glove.ino
#include <Arduino.h>
#include <Wire.h>
#include <Adafruit_MPU6050.h>
#include <Adafruit_Sensor.h>
#include <BLEDevice.h>
#include <BLEServer.h>
#include <math.h>
#include "Mpu6500.h"

const char *SERVICE = "60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000001";
const char *DATA = "60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000002";
Adafruit_MPU6050 mpu;
Mpu6500 mpu6500;
bool using6500=false;
BLECharacteristic *dataChar;
BLEServer *server;
volatile bool restartAdvertising = false;
volatile bool peerConnected = false;
uint32_t lastStatus = 0;
uint8_t sensorAddress = 0x68;
float zeroRoll = 0, zeroPitch = 0, roll = 0, pitch = 0;
uint32_t sequence = 0;

class Callbacks : public BLEServerCallbacks {
  void onConnect(BLEServer *) override { peerConnected=true; }
  void onDisconnect(BLEServer *) override { peerConnected=false; restartAdvertising = true; }
};

bool angles(float &r, float &p) {
  sensors_event_t a, g, t;
  bool valid=using6500 ? mpu6500.getEvent(&a,&g,&t) : mpu.getEvent(&a,&g,&t);
  if (!valid) return false;
  r = atan2f(a.acceleration.y, a.acceleration.z) * 180.0f / PI;
  p = atan2f(-a.acceleration.x,
       sqrtf(a.acceleration.y*a.acceleration.y + a.acceleration.z*a.acceleration.z)) * 180.0f / PI;
  return isfinite(r) && isfinite(p);
}

void calibrate() {
  Serial.println("Hold glove flat and still for calibration.");
  float sumR = 0, sumP = 0;
  int samples = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
    float r, p;
    if (angles(r, p)) { sumR += r; sumP += p; ++samples; }
    delay(10);
  }
  if (samples) { zeroRoll = sumR/samples; zeroPitch = sumP/samples; }
  roll = pitch = 0;
  Serial.printf("Calibration samples=%d neutralRoll=%.2f neutralPitch=%.2f\n",samples,zeroRoll,zeroPitch);
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  Wire.begin(21, 22);
  Wire.setTimeOut(25);
  bool sensorReady=false;
  while (!sensorReady) {
    for (uint8_t address : {0x68,0x69}) {
      sensorAddress=address;
      if (mpu.begin(address)) { sensorReady=true; break; }
      if (mpu6500.begin(address)) { using6500=true; sensorReady=true; break; }
    }
    if (!sensorReady) {
      Serial.printf("GLOVE I2C scan SDAlevel=%d SCLlevel=%d\n",digitalRead(21),digitalRead(22));
      int found=0;
      for (uint8_t address=1;address<127;++address) {
        Wire.beginTransmission(address);
        if (Wire.endTransmission()==0) {
          ++found; Serial.printf("GLOVE I2C ACK address=0x%02X\n",address);
          if (address==0x68 || address==0x69) {
            Wire.beginTransmission(address); Wire.write(0x75);
            if (Wire.endTransmission(false)==0 && Wire.requestFrom(address,(uint8_t)1)==1)
              Serial.printf("GLOVE WHO_AM_I=0x%02X (MPU6050 expected 0x68)\n",Wire.read());
          }
        }
      }
      Serial.printf("GLOVE I2C devices=%d; MPU6050/MPU6500 init failed; retrying in 3 seconds\n",found);
      delay(3000);
    }
  }
  Serial.printf("%s detected at 0x%02X\n",using6500?"MPU6500":"MPU6050",sensorAddress);
  if (!using6500) {
    mpu.setAccelerometerRange(MPU6050_RANGE_4_G);
    mpu.setFilterBandwidth(MPU6050_BAND_21_HZ);
  }
  calibrate();
  BLEDevice::init("GestureGlove");
  Serial.printf("Glove BLE address: %s\n",BLEDevice::getAddress().toString().c_str());
  server = BLEDevice::createServer();
  server->setCallbacks(new Callbacks());
  BLEService *service = server->createService(SERVICE);
  dataChar = service->createCharacteristic(DATA, BLECharacteristic::PROPERTY_READ);
  dataChar->setValue("0,90,90");
  service->start();
  BLEDevice::getAdvertising()->addServiceUUID(SERVICE);
  BLEDevice::getAdvertising()->setScanResponse(true);
  BLEDevice::startAdvertising();
  Serial.println("Ready. Send c in Serial Monitor to recalibrate.");
}

void loop() {
  if (restartAdvertising) {
    restartAdvertising = false;
    BLEDevice::startAdvertising();
  }
  if (Serial.available() && Serial.read() == 'c') calibrate();
  float r, p;
  if (angles(r, p)) {
    float delta = r-zeroRoll;
    while (delta > 180) delta -= 360;
    while (delta < -180) delta += 360;
    roll += 0.2f*(delta-roll);
    pitch += 0.2f*(p-zeroPitch-pitch);
    // Roll steers pan; pitch steers tilt. Invert either sign if necessary.
    int pan = constrain((int)lroundf(90 + roll), 30, 150);
    int tilt = constrain((int)lroundf(90 + pitch), 45, 135);
    char packet[20];
    snprintf(packet, sizeof(packet), "%lu,%d,%d", (unsigned long)++sequence, pan, tilt);
    dataChar->setValue(packet);
    if (millis()-lastStatus>=500) {
      lastStatus=millis();
      Serial.printf("GLOVE sensor=OK seq=%lu roll=%.1f pitch=%.1f pan=%d tilt=%d BLE=%s\n",
        (unsigned long)sequence,roll,pitch,pan,tilt,peerConnected?"CONNECTED":"ADVERTISING");
    }
  } else if (millis()-lastStatus>=1000) {
    lastStatus=millis(); Serial.println("GLOVE sensor read failed; command sequence not updated");
  }
  delay(40);
}
turret/WheelDrive.h
#pragma once
#include <Arduino.h>

// Proposed L298N wiring for this original ESP32: remove ENA/ENB jumpers.
// Two motors per side, only when the driver's current rating allows it.
class WheelDrive {
 public:
  static constexpr int IN1=14, IN2=16, IN3=17, IN4=26, ENA=2, ENB=15;
  static constexpr int MAX_PWM=120; // 0..255; initial limit for bench bring-up
  static constexpr bool INVERT_LEFT=false, INVERT_RIGHT=false;

  bool begin() {
    for (int pin : {IN1,IN2,IN3,IN4,ENA,ENB}) {
      pinMode(pin,OUTPUT); digitalWrite(pin,LOW);
    }
    // Reserve channels in a separate timer from the servo channels.
    bool a=ledcAttachChannel(ENA,5000,8,14);
    bool b=ledcAttachChannel(ENB,5000,8,15);
    ready=a && b;
    if (a) ledcWrite(ENA,0);
    if (b) ledcWrite(ENB,0);
    if (!ready) return false;
    ready = xTaskCreate(taskEntry,"wheel-output",3072,this,2,nullptr)==pdPASS;
    return ready;
  }

  void mode(bool on) {
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&mux);
    enabled=on && ready; armed=false; neutralSince=0; left=right=0; jogging=false;
    updatedAt=millis();
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux);
  }

  void update(bool live,int pan,int tilt) {
    uint32_t now=millis();
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&mux);
    // Any update gap also requires a fresh neutral hold before movement.
    if (now-updatedAt>250 || !live || !enabled) {
      armed=false; neutralSince=0;
    }
    updatedAt=now;
    left=right=0;
    if (enabled && live) {
      bool neutral=abs(pan-90)<=8 && abs(tilt-90)<=8;
      if (!armed) {
        if (!neutral) neutralSince=0;
        else if (!neutralSince) neutralSince=now;
        else if (now-neutralSince>=500) armed=true;
      }
      if (armed) {
        int throttle=axis(90-tilt,45); // forward glove pitch => forward wheels
        int steer=axis(pan-90,60);
        int l=throttle+steer, r=throttle-steer;
        int peak=max(abs(l),abs(r));
        if (peak>MAX_PWM) { l=l*MAX_PWM/peak; r=r*MAX_PWM/peak; }
        left=INVERT_LEFT ? -l:l; right=INVERT_RIGHT ? -r:r;
      }
    }
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux);
  }

  bool isArmed() {
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&mux); bool value=armed; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux);
    return value;
  }

  bool testPulse(int l,int r,uint32_t duration=200) {
    if (!ready) return false;
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&mux);
    enabled=false; armed=false; neutralSince=0; left=right=0;
    jogLeft=constrain(l,-180,180); jogRight=constrain(r,-180,180);
    if (INVERT_LEFT) jogLeft=-jogLeft;
    if (INVERT_RIGHT) jogRight=-jogRight;
    jogUntil=millis()+constrain(duration,(uint32_t)1,(uint32_t)1500); jogging=true;
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&mux);
    return true;
  }

 private:
  portMUX_TYPE mux=portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED;
  bool ready=false, enabled=false, armed=false;
  int left=0,right=0;
  uint32_t updatedAt=0,neutralSince=0;
  bool jogging=false;
  int jogLeft=0,jogRight=0;
  uint32_t jogUntil=0;
  struct Side { int sign=0; uint32_t offSince=0; bool powered=false; };
  Side leftState,rightState;

  static int axis(int angle,int range) {
    int magnitude=abs(angle);
    if (magnitude<=8) return 0;
    int pwm=constrain((magnitude-8)*MAX_PWM/(range-8),0,MAX_PWM);
    return angle<0 ? -pwm:pwm;
  }

  static void output(Side &side,int pwm,int en,int a,int b) {
    uint32_t now=millis();
    int sign=(pwm>0)-(pwm<0);
    if (!sign || (side.sign && sign!=side.sign)) {
      ledcWrite(en,0); digitalWrite(a,LOW); digitalWrite(b,LOW);
      if (side.powered) { side.offSince=now; side.powered=false; }
      // Leave at least 150ms with the bridge disabled before reversing.
      if (!sign || now-side.offSince<150) return;
    }
    digitalWrite(a,sign>0); digitalWrite(b,sign<0);
    side.sign=sign; side.powered=true; ledcWrite(en,abs(pwm));
  }

  static void taskEntry(void *argument) {
    auto *self=static_cast<WheelDrive *>(argument);
    for (;;) {
      int l=0,r=0;
      portENTER_CRITICAL(&self->mux);
      if (millis()-self->updatedAt>250) {
        self->armed=false; self->neutralSince=0;
      }
      if (self->enabled && self->armed) { l=self->left; r=self->right; }
      if (self->jogging) {
        if ((int32_t)(millis()-self->jogUntil)>=0) self->jogging=false;
        else { l=self->jogLeft; r=self->jogRight; }
      }
      portEXIT_CRITICAL(&self->mux);
      output(self->leftState,l,ENA,IN1,IN2);
      output(self->rightState,r,ENB,IN3,IN4);
      vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));
    }
  }
};
turret/turret.ino
#include <Arduino.h>
#include <Wire.h>
#include <ESP32Servo.h>
#include <Adafruit_GFX.h>
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
#include <BLEDevice.h>
#include <BLEClient.h>
#include <BLEScan.h>
#include "WheelDrive.h"

const char *SERVICE = "60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000001";
const char *DATA = "60184255-b28e-4200-a001-000000000002";
constexpr int PAN=13, TILT=27, TRIG=5, ECHO=18, PIR=19;
constexpr int LASER=23, BUZZER=25, RED=32, GREEN=33, BLUE=4;
// These outputs drive module logic inputs or transistor drivers, never loads.
constexpr bool RGB_COMMON_ANODE = false;
constexpr uint8_t OLED_ADDRESS = 0x3C;
constexpr bool PASSIVE_BUZZER = false; // true: tone(); false: active buzzer
Servo panServo, tiltServo;
WheelDrive wheels;
bool driveMode=false;
int glovePan=90, gloveTilt=90;
Adafruit_SSD1306 display(128, 64, &Wire, -1);
bool oledOK=false, holdPosition=false, motion=false, nearObject=false;
BLEClient *client;
BLERemoteCharacteristic *remoteData=nullptr;
int pan=90, tilt=90, targetPan=90, targetTilt=90;
float distanceCm=-1;
uint32_t lastPacket=0, lastSequence=0, laserUntil=0;
uint32_t lastRead=0, lastServo=0, lastSense=0, lastDisplay=0, lastScan=0;
bool haveSequence=false, laserOn=false;
bool diagnostic=false;
uint32_t diagnosticStarted=0;
int diagnosticPhase=-1;

void rgb(bool r, bool g, bool b) {
  digitalWrite(RED, r != RGB_COMMON_ANODE);
  digitalWrite(GREEN, g != RGB_COMMON_ANODE);
  digitalWrite(BLUE, b != RGB_COMMON_ANODE);
}
void buzzer(bool on) {
  if (PASSIVE_BUZZER) { if (on) tone(BUZZER, 2000); else noTone(BUZZER); }
  else digitalWrite(BUZZER, on);
}
void laserOff() { digitalWrite(LASER, LOW); laserOn=false; }
bool fresh() {
  return client && client->isConnected() && haveSequence && millis()-lastPacket < 300;
}

void connectGlove() {
  laserOff();
  wheels.update(false,90,90);
  buzzer(false);
  remoteData=nullptr;
  haveSequence=false;
  BLEScan *scan = BLEDevice::getScan();
  scan->setActiveScan(true);
  // Synchronous scan: outputs remain off; servos hold during reconnection.
  auto results = scan->start(1, false);
  (void)results;
  BLEScanResults *found = scan->getResults();
  for (int i=0; i<found->getCount(); ++i) {
    BLEAdvertisedDevice device = found->getDevice(i);
    if (!device.haveServiceUUID() || !device.isAdvertisingService(BLEUUID(SERVICE))) continue;
    if (client->connect(&device)) {
      BLERemoteService *service = client->getService(SERVICE);
      if (service) remoteData = service->getCharacteristic(DATA);
      if (!remoteData || !remoteData->canRead()) {
        remoteData=nullptr;
        client->disconnect();
      }
    }
    break;
  }
  scan->clearResults();
}

void readGlove() {
  if (!client->isConnected() || !remoteData) return;
  auto value = remoteData->readValue();
  unsigned long seq;
  int p,t, consumed=0;
  if (sscanf(value.c_str(), "%lu,%d,%d%n", &seq,&p,&t,&consumed) != 3 ||
      consumed != (int)value.length() || p<30 || p>150 || t<45 || t>135) return;
  if (!haveSequence || seq != lastSequence) {
    lastSequence=seq; haveSequence=true; lastPacket=millis();
    glovePan=p; gloveTilt=t;
    if (!holdPosition && !driveMode) { targetPan=p; targetTilt=t; }
  }
}

void sense() {
  digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW); delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(TRIG, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10); digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW);
  unsigned long duration = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH, 25000);
  distanceCm = duration ? duration * 0.0343f / 2 : -1;
  // HC-SR501 needs about 60 seconds to settle after power-up.
  motion = millis()>60000 && digitalRead(PIR);
  nearObject = distanceCm>0 && distanceCm<30;
}

void scanBus() {
  Serial.println("I2C scan (turret SDA21/SCL22):");
  int count=0;
  for (uint8_t address=1;address<127;++address) {
    Wire.beginTransmission(address);
    if (Wire.endTransmission()==0) {
      Serial.printf("I2C ACK 0x%02X\n",address); ++count;
    }
  }
  Serial.printf("I2C devices=%d OLED buffer=%d servoPanHz=%lu servoTiltHz=%lu wheelAHz=%lu wheelBHz=%lu\n",
    count,oledOK,(unsigned long)ledcReadFreq(PAN),(unsigned long)ledcReadFreq(TILT),(unsigned long)ledcReadFreq(WheelDrive::ENA),(unsigned long)ledcReadFreq(WheelDrive::ENB));
  Serial.printf("I2C diagnostic uptime=%lu PIRraw=%d PIRwarmup=%d servoAttached=%d/%d wheelDuty=%lu/%lu\n",
    (unsigned long)millis(),digitalRead(PIR),millis()<60000,panServo.attached(),tiltServo.attached(),
    (unsigned long)ledcRead(WheelDrive::ENA),(unsigned long)ledcRead(WheelDrive::ENB));
  Serial.println("ACK/configuration does not prove visible display or physical movement.");
}

void diagnosticTick(uint32_t now) {
  int phase=(now-diagnosticStarted)/1000;
  if (phase==diagnosticPhase) return;
  diagnosticPhase=phase;
  buzzer(false); rgb(false,false,false);
  switch (phase) {
    case 0: Serial.println("TEST RGB RED + OLED text"); rgb(true,false,false); break;
    case 1: Serial.println("TEST RGB GREEN"); rgb(false,true,false); break;
    case 2: Serial.println("TEST RGB BLUE"); rgb(false,false,true); break;
    case 3: Serial.println("TEST BUZZER 150ms"); break;
    case 4: Serial.println("TEST PAN -> 80 degrees"); targetPan=80; break;
    case 5: Serial.println("TEST PAN -> 100 degrees"); targetPan=100; break;
    case 6: Serial.println("TEST PAN -> 90 degrees"); targetPan=90; break;
    case 7: Serial.println("TEST TILT -> 80 degrees"); targetTilt=80; break;
    case 8: Serial.println("TEST TILT -> 100 degrees"); targetTilt=100; break;
    case 9: Serial.println("TEST TILT -> 90 degrees"); targetTilt=90; break;
    default:
      diagnostic=false; targetPan=targetTilt=90;
      Serial.println("TEST sequence complete; wheels disabled, laser off. Confirm visible/light/sound responses."); break;
  }
}

void commands() {
  while (Serial.available()) {
    char command=Serial.read();
    switch (command) {
      case 'U': case 'V': case 'J': case 'K': {
        diagnostic=false; driveMode=false; holdPosition=true;
        targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; laserOff(); wheels.mode(false);
        int l=command=='U' ? 180 : command=='J' ? -180 : 0;
        int r=command=='V' ? 180 : command=='K' ? -180 : 0;
        Serial.printf("TEST WHEEL %s %s 1500ms duty180 accepted=%d\n",
          l ? "LEFT":"RIGHT", (l+r)>0 ? "forward":"reverse", wheels.testPulse(l,r,1500));
        break;
      }
      case 'p':
        Serial.printf("WHEEL pins IN1=%d IN2=%d IN3=%d IN4=%d ENA=%lu ENB=%lu armed=%d\n",
          digitalRead(WheelDrive::IN1),digitalRead(WheelDrive::IN2),digitalRead(WheelDrive::IN3),digitalRead(WheelDrive::IN4),
          (unsigned long)ledcRead(WheelDrive::ENA),(unsigned long)ledcRead(WheelDrive::ENB),wheels.isArmed());
        break;
      case 'u':
        diagnostic=false; driveMode=false; holdPosition=true;
        targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; laserOff(); wheels.mode(false);
        Serial.println(wheels.testPulse(80,0) ? "TEST WHEEL LEFT forward 200ms duty80" : "TEST WHEEL FAILED: PWM unavailable");
        break;
      case 'v':
        diagnostic=false; driveMode=false; holdPosition=true;
        targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; laserOff(); wheels.mode(false);
        Serial.println(wheels.testPulse(0,80) ? "TEST WHEEL RIGHT forward 200ms duty80" : "TEST WHEEL FAILED: PWM unavailable");
        break;
      case 'i': scanBus(); break;
      case 't':
        driveMode=false; wheels.mode(false); holdPosition=true; laserOff();
        targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; diagnostic=true;
        diagnosticStarted=millis(); diagnosticPhase=-1;
        Serial.println("TEST starting: RGB/OLED/buzzer/servos; wheels and laser remain OFF");
        scanBus(); diagnosticStarted=millis(); break;
      case 's':
      case 'h': diagnostic=false; buzzer(false); driveMode=false; wheels.mode(false); holdPosition=true; targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; laserOff(); break;
      case 'd': diagnostic=false; driveMode=true; wheels.mode(true); holdPosition=true; targetPan=pan; targetTilt=tilt; laserOff(); break;
      case 'g': diagnostic=false; driveMode=false; wheels.mode(false); holdPosition=false; break;
      case 'c': diagnostic=false; driveMode=false; wheels.mode(false); holdPosition=true; targetPan=targetTilt=90; laserOff(); break;
      case 'l': // Manual one-second pulse, only with a live glove link.
        if (fresh() && !holdPosition) {
          laserUntil=millis()+1000; laserOn=true; digitalWrite(LASER,HIGH);
        }
        break;
      case '0': laserOff(); break;
    }
  }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  for (int pin : {TRIG,LASER,BUZZER,RED,GREEN,BLUE}) pinMode(pin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(ECHO,INPUT); pinMode(PIR,INPUT);
  laserOff(); buzzer(false); rgb(false,false,true);
  Wire.begin(21,22);
  Wire.setTimeOut(25);
  oledOK=display.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC, OLED_ADDRESS);
  panServo.setPeriodHertz(50); tiltServo.setPeriodHertz(50);
  // Conservative pulse range; calibrate to your servo and mechanical limits.
  panServo.attach(PAN,1000,2000); tiltServo.attach(TILT,1000,2000);
  panServo.write(pan); tiltServo.write(tilt);
  Serial.println(wheels.begin() ? "Wheel PWM ready (L298N); wheels disarmed" : "Wheel PWM initialization FAILED; drive disabled");
  BLEDevice::init("GestureTurret");
  client=BLEDevice::createClient();
  Serial.println("d=wheel mode g=turret mode s=stop h=hold c=center l=laser 1s 0=laser off i=I2C scan t=hardware test");
}

void loop() {
  commands();
  uint32_t now=millis();
  if (laserOn && (!fresh() || holdPosition || (int32_t)(now-laserUntil)>=0)) laserOff();
  if (!diagnostic && !client->isConnected() && now-lastScan>=2000) {
    lastScan=now; connectGlove(); now=millis();
  }
  if (!diagnostic && now-lastRead>=50) { lastRead=now; readGlove(); now=millis(); }
  if (now-lastSense>=150) { lastSense=now; sense(); now=millis(); }
  bool live=fresh();
  wheels.update(live,glovePan,gloveTilt);
  if (!live) laserOff();
  if (diagnostic) diagnosticTick(now);
  if (now-lastServo>=20) {
    lastServo=now;
    // Center is allowed in hold mode; otherwise hold the last position on loss.
    if (live || holdPosition) {
      if (pan<targetPan) ++pan; else if (pan>targetPan) --pan;
      if (tilt<targetTilt) ++tilt; else if (tilt>targetTilt) --tilt;
      panServo.write(pan); tiltServo.write(tilt);
    }
  }
  bool alert=motion || nearObject;
  if (diagnostic) buzzer(diagnosticPhase==3 && (now-diagnosticStarted)%1000<150);
  else {
    buzzer(alert && (now%1000)<100);
    rgb(alert,live && !alert,!live && !alert);
  }
  if (now-lastDisplay>=250) {
    lastDisplay=now;
    if (oledOK) {
      display.clearDisplay(); display.setTextColor(SSD1306_WHITE); display.setTextSize(1); display.setCursor(0,0);
      if (diagnostic) { display.println("HARDWARE TEST"); display.printf("Step: %d/10\n",diagnosticPhase+1); }
      else display.println(!live ? "GLOVE LINK LOST" : driveMode ? (wheels.isArmed() ? "DRIVE" : "DRIVE: HOLD NEUTRAL") : holdPosition ? "HOLD" : "TURRET");
      display.printf("Pan:%d Tilt:%d\n",pan,tilt);
      if (distanceCm<0) display.println("Range: no echo");
      else display.printf("Range: %.1f cm\n",distanceCm);
      display.printf("PIR:%s Near:%s\n",motion?"YES":"no",nearObject?"YES":"no");
      display.printf("Laser:%s\n",laserOn?"ON":"OFF");
      display.display();
    }
    Serial.printf("link=%d mode=%s armed=%d pan=%d tilt=%d cm=%.1f PIR=%d\n",live,driveMode?"DRIVE":"TURRET",wheels.isArmed(),pan,tilt,distanceCm,motion);
  }
  delay(2);
}

test_devices.py
"""Run the bounded peripheral diagnostic; leaves wheels disarmed and laser off.

Use .venv/bin/python test_devices.py with the main ESP32 connected over USB.
Watch the hardware: serial confirms output commands, not physical actuation.
"""
import datetime
from pathlib import Path
import time
import serial

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
lines = []
port = serial.Serial()
port.port = "/dev/cu.usbserial-0001"
port.baudrate = 115200
port.timeout = 0.2
port.dtr = False
port.rts = False

def collect(seconds):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        raw = port.readline().decode("ascii", errors="ignore").strip()
        # Discard startup UART noise while preserving diagnostic/status text.
        markers = ("link=", "TEST ", "I2C ", "ACK/configuration", "Wheel PWM")
        offsets = [raw.find(marker) for marker in markers if marker in raw]
        if offsets:
            line = raw[min(offsets):]
            lines.append(line)
            print(line, flush=True)

try:
    port.open()
    port.reset_input_buffer()
    port.write(b"s\n0\n")
    collect(3)
    port.write(b"t\n")
    collect(15)
    port.write(b"i\n")
    collect(3)
finally:
    if port.is_open:
        port.write(b"s\n0\n")
        port.flush()
        port.close()
    log = root / "device-test.log"
    log.write_text(datetime.datetime.now().isoformat() + "\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"Log saved: {log}")
test_wheels.py
"""Explicit bench test: lift wheels first. Pulses each side for 200ms.

Requires the proposed L298N wiring in WHEELS.md. Output commands and PWM
configuration are observable over serial; physical rotation is not sensed.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import time
import serial

port=serial.Serial()
port.port='/dev/cu.usbserial-0001'
port.baudrate=115200
port.timeout=0.02
port.dtr=False
port.rts=False
lines=[]

def collect(seconds):
    end=time.monotonic()+seconds
    while time.monotonic()<end:
        raw=port.readline().decode('ascii',errors='ignore').strip()
        markers=('TEST WHEEL','I2C ','link=','Wheel PWM')
        offsets=[raw.find(x) for x in markers if x in raw]
        if offsets:
            line=raw[min(offsets):]
            lines.append(line)
            if not line.startswith('link='):
                print(line,flush=True)

try:
    port.open()
    port.reset_input_buffer()
    collect(4)
    port.write(b's\n0\n')
    collect(1)
    for command,side in ((b'u\n','LEFT'),(b'v\n','RIGHT')):
        print(f'Running {side}: 200ms at duty 80/255',flush=True)
        port.write(command)
        collect(0.04)
        port.write(b'i\n')
        collect(2)
    port.write(b's\n0\ni\n')
    collect(3)
finally:
    if port.is_open:
        port.write(b's\n0\n')
        port.flush()
        port.close()
    path=Path(__file__).with_name('wheel-test.log')
    path.write_text('\n'.join(lines)+'\n')
    print(f'Wheels commanded STOP. Log: {path}',flush=True)
test_wheels_extended.py
"""Explicit lifted-wheel bench test; 1.5s per side/direction at duty180.

Requires updated firmware and L298N mapping in WHEELS.md. Serial snapshots
verify configured GPIO levels/PWM only, not voltages at the driver or motion.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import time
import serial

port=serial.Serial()
port.port='/dev/cu.usbserial-0001'
port.baudrate=115200
port.timeout=0.02
port.dtr=False
port.rts=False
lines=[]
stop_sent=False

def collect(seconds):
    captured=[]
    end=time.monotonic()+seconds
    while time.monotonic()<end:
        raw=port.readline().decode('ascii',errors='ignore').strip()
        offsets=[raw.find(x) for x in ('TEST WHEEL','WHEEL pins','link=','Wheel PWM') if x in raw]
        if offsets:
            line=raw[min(offsets):]
            lines.append(line);captured.append(line)
            if not line.startswith('link='): print(line,flush=True)
    return captured

def snapshot():
    port.write(b'p\n')
    return collect(1.3)

try:
    port.open();port.reset_input_buffer()
    collect(4)
    port.write(b's\n0\n');collect(1)
    checks=[]
    phases=((b'U\n','LEFT FORWARD',(1,0,0,0,180,0)),
            (b'V\n','RIGHT FORWARD',(0,0,1,0,0,180)),
            (b'J\n','LEFT REVERSE',(0,1,0,0,180,0)),
            (b'K\n','RIGHT REVERSE',(0,0,0,1,0,180)))
    for command,label,expected in phases:
        print(f'RUN {label}: 1500ms, duty180/255',flush=True)
        port.write(command)
        acknowledged=False
        deadline=time.monotonic()+4
        while time.monotonic()<deadline:
            if any('TEST WHEEL ' in line and 'accepted=1' in line for line in collect(0.05)):
                acknowledged=True
                break
        if not acknowledged:
            print('No accepted-command acknowledgement; aborting.',flush=True)
            checks.append(False)
            break
        started=time.monotonic()
        captured=[]
        # Poll through the whole pulse. BLE may delay serial processing, so
        # zero snapshots at the edges are allowed; nonzero wrong states fail.
        while time.monotonic()-started<1.7:
            port.write(b'p\n')
            captured+=collect(0.18)
        samples=[]
        for line in captured:
            match=re.search(r'IN1=(\d) IN2=(\d) IN3=(\d) IN4=(\d) ENA=(\d+) ENB=(\d+)',line)
            if match: samples.append(tuple(map(int,match.groups())))
        active=[sample for sample in samples if sample[4] or sample[5]]
        valid=bool(active) and all(sample==expected for sample in active)
        print(f'GPIO/PWM check {label}: {"PASS" if valid else "FAIL/NO ACTIVE SAMPLE"}',flush=True)
        checks.append(valid)
        collect(0.4)
        stopped=snapshot()
        valid=any('ENA=0 ENB=0' in line for line in stopped)
        print(f'Expiry check: {"PASS" if valid else "FAIL"}',flush=True)
        checks.append(valid)
        if not all(checks):
            print('Aborting remaining phases after unexpected status.',flush=True)
            break
        collect(0.3)
    port.write(b's\n0\n');collect(0.4)
    snapshot()
    print('ALL OUTPUT CHECKS PASSED' if checks and all(checks) else 'OUTPUT CHECKS INCOMPLETE/FAILED',flush=True)
finally:
    if port.is_open:
        port.write(b's\n0\n');port.flush();stop_sent=True;port.close()
    log=Path(__file__).with_name('wheel-test-extended.log')
    if lines:
        log.write_text('\n'.join(lines)+'\n')
    print(f'Stop and laser-off commands sent. Log: {log}' if stop_sent else 'Port could not be opened; no test or stop commands were sent.',flush=True)

#include <cassert>
#include <iostream>
#include "../turret/WheelDrive.h"
int main() {
  WheelDrive w;
  assert(w.begin()); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  assert(w.testPulse(80,0)); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==80 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  fakeNow+=201; tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0 && !w.isArmed());
  assert(w.testPulse(0,80)); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==80);
  w.mode(false); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  w.mode(true);
  for (int i=0;i<8;++i) { fakeNow+=100; w.update(true,90,45); tick(); }
  assert(!w.isArmed() && duty[w.ENA]==0); // tilted glove cannot arm
  for (int i=0;i<7;++i) { fakeNow+=100; w.update(true,90,90); tick(); }
  assert(w.isArmed());
  w.update(true,90,45); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==120 && duty[w.ENB]==120);
  assert(pins[w.IN1]==HIGH && pins[w.IN2]==LOW);
  fakeNow+=10; w.update(true,90,135); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0); // reversal dead time
  fakeNow+=100; w.update(true,90,135); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0);
  fakeNow+=50; w.update(true,90,135); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==120 && pins[w.IN1]==LOW && pins[w.IN2]==HIGH);
  fakeNow+=251; tick(); // no loop updates: independent watchdog stops wheels
  assert(!w.isArmed() && duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  w.update(true,150,45); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0); // requires neutral again after timeout
  for (int i=0;i<7;++i) { fakeNow+=100; w.update(true,90,90); tick(); }
  w.update(true,150,45); tick();
  fakeNow+=160; w.update(true,150,45); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]<=120 && duty[w.ENB]<=120); // mixed steering capped
  w.update(false,90,45); tick();
  assert(!w.isArmed() && duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  w.mode(false); w.update(true,90,45); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  assert(w.testPulse(255,0,10000)); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==180 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  fakeNow+=1499; tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==180);
  fakeNow+=2; tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  assert(w.testPulse(0,-180,1500)); tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENB]==180); // side has already been off for more than 150ms
  fakeNow+=160; tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENB]==180 && pins[w.IN3]==LOW && pins[w.IN4]==HIGH);
  fakeNow+=1341; tick();
  assert(duty[w.ENA]==0 && duty[w.ENB]==0);
  std::cout << "PASS: startup, neutral arming, drive, reversal delay, watchdog, rearming, speed cap, link loss, stop\n";
}

README.md
# Gesture sentry: two ESP32 sketches

**Wheel support added:** see [WHEELS.md](WHEELS.md) for the proposed L298N wiring and drive-mode controls.

Target: two original ESP32/WROOM-32 development boards, Arduino IDE, Arduino-ESP32 **3.x**. Boards such as ESP32-C3/S3 have different pins; this wiring is not interchangeable.

## Install and upload

Install **esp32 by Espressif Systems** in Boards Manager. Install these Library Manager libraries and accept their dependencies:

- ESP32Servo
- Adafruit MPU6050
- Adafruit Unified Sensor
- Adafruit SSD1306
- Adafruit GFX Library

BLE and Wire come with the ESP32 board package. Select **ESP32 Dev Module** and the appropriate USB port. Open `glove/glove.ino` and upload to the glove board. Open `turret/turret.ino` and upload to the turret board. Open Serial Monitor at **115200 baud**. Both sketches were compiled successfully on 2026-10-26 using Arduino-ESP32 3.3.12. The turret sketch was uploaded to ESP32-D0WD-V3 (MAC d4:8a:fc:61:62:f8) at /dev/cu.usbserial-0001; the uploader verified the flash hashes. Runtime serial output confirmed the main loop is running. The glove sketch was subsequently compiled and uploaded to the second ESP32 (MAC 20:9b:a9:99:28:5c) at 115200 baud with flash hash verification. Runtime reports MPU6050 initialization failure at both 0x68/0x69; BLE startup is held until the sensor initializes. Full peripheral operation is not yet verified.

## Wiring

Turret connections:

| Device | Connection |
|---|---|
| MG995 pan | Signal GPIO13; power external regulated 5V; GND common |
| SG90 tilt | Signal GPIO27; power external regulated 5V; GND common |
| HC-SR04 | TRIG GPIO5; ECHO through divider to GPIO18; VCC 5V; GND common |
| HC-SR501 PIR | OUT GPIO19; VCC 5V; GND common |
| OLED SSD1306 128x64 I2C | SDA GPIO21; SCL GPIO22; VCC 3.3V; GND common |
| RGB module | R GPIO32; G GPIO33; B GPIO4; GND common, assuming common cathode and onboard resistors |
| Laser module | Logic input S GPIO23 only if rated for 3.3V logic; supply per module rating; GND common |
| 5V buzzer | GPIO25 to transistor driver input; buzzer powered from 5V through driver |

HC-SR04 divider: **ECHO → 1kΩ → GPIO18 junction → 2kΩ → GND**. Never connect its 5V ECHO directly to GPIO18.

For an active buzzer, use an NPN transistor: GPIO25 → 1kΩ → base, emitter → GND, collector → buzzer negative, buzzer positive → 5V. Add a 10kΩ base-to-ground resistor. For a magnetic buzzer, add the appropriate flyback diode across it, cathode to +5V. The default code assumes an active buzzer; set `PASSIVE_BUZZER=true` for a passive one using a suitable driver.

If the laser module has only two wires, GPIO23 must control a transistor/MOSFET driver instead of powering it directly. Its exact supply voltage and switching arrangement depend on the actual module. Add a pull-down on the driver input so it remains off during boot. Use only a low-power visible indicator module and keep the beam away from eyes and reflective surfaces.

The diagram's second RGB module is not separately assigned any GPIOs. This implementation controls the one mapped module. An additional independently controlled RGB needs three additional pins and its actual module wiring.

Glove MPU6050/GY-521: **VCC→3.3V, GND→GND, SDA→GPIO21, SCL→GPIO22, AD0→GND**. INT is unused. Power the glove board by USB initially.

Use an external regulated **5V supply sized for both servos' combined peak/stall current**, with its ground connected to turret ESP32 GND. Power the turret ESP32 over USB for initial testing. Do not draw servo power from the ESP32 3V3 pin or through its USB/board regulator. Do not connect an unknown four-cell holder directly to VIN; determine its topology and use an appropriate regulator and protected battery arrangement first. Do not connect USB 5V and an external 5V rail together unless your particular board provides suitable power isolation. Software cannot fix the missing battery regulator/charging hardware.

## Operation

1. Initially disconnect servo horns/linkages. Boot the glove flat and still: it calibrates for one second.
2. Boot the turret. BLE connects automatically; the servos start at 90°. Fit horns only after confirming center. Start with the laser disconnected.
3. Roll the glove left/right to pan; pitch forward/back to tilt. This uses gravity-based tilt, not compass heading or drift-free yaw. Reverse the signs in the glove mapping if movement is backwards.
4. The code restricts pan to 30–150° and tilt to 45–135°, using conservative 1000–2000µs servo pulses. Reduce travel further if the mechanism binds. Servo models vary; calibrate these limits for your build.
5. OLED shows link, angles, range, PIR and laser state. Green = connected, blue = link unavailable, red = PIR motion or an object closer than 30cm. Alerts sound a short beep each second. PIR is ignored for the first 60 seconds while it settles. No ultrasonic echo is reported as unavailable, not clear space.
6. Stale glove data for 300ms or disconnection holds the servos and turns the laser off. BLE scanning/reconnection is synchronous and can pause sensing/display updates. Sensors only trigger indicators; they do not aim the mechanism or activate the laser.

Turret Serial Monitor commands:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `g` | Resume gesture control |
| `h` | Hold current servo position; laser off |
| `c` | Move gradually to center and stay in hold mode |
| `l` | Manually activate laser for one second, only with a fresh glove link and gesture mode |
| `0` | Laser off immediately when processed |

Glove Serial Monitor: `c` recalibrates neutral while the glove is still. Recalibration interrupts updates, so the turret may briefly report a lost link.

The BLE link is a simple unauthenticated demonstration. It does not implement pairing or restrict connections to a particular glove. The manual hold command is not a physical emergency stop. L298N wheel control has now been added on a proposed pin mapping; see WHEELS.md. The actual motor-controller model has not been confirmed.

## Troubleshooting

- OLED blank: check whether your actual display uses address 0x3D rather than 0x3C, resolution 128x32 rather than 128x64, or an SH1106 rather than SSD1306 controller; change the configuration/library accordingly.
- MPU missing: verify power, shared ground, SDA/SCL and AD0. The glove code tries addresses 0x68 and 0x69; AD0 grounded selects 0x68. Initialization also checks the sensor identity, so another sensor model needs a matching library.
- Resets or servo jitter: check the external supply and common ground, and add appropriate bulk capacitance near the servo rail.
- RGB inverted: set `RGB_COMMON_ANODE=true` and connect the module common to its specified supply. Bare LEDs need individual current-limiting resistors; 5V RGB boards may need drivers.
- No buzzer sound: verify active/passive type and driver wiring.

API references: [Espressif BLE](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/arduino-esp32/en/latest/api/ble.html), [ESP32Servo](https://github.com/madhephaestus/ESP32Servo), [Adafruit MPU6050](https://adafruit.github.io/Adafruit_MPU6050/html/class_adafruit___m_p_u6050.html).

## Latest device check (2026-10-26)

The running main board reported `link=0 pan=90 tilt=90 cm=-1.0 PIR=0`: glove unavailable, servos commanded to center, no ultrasonic echo, PIR inactive. These are software status reports, not confirmation of mechanical movement or sensor wiring. The initial check preceded wheel support; see WHEELS.md for the subsequently added proposed L298N layout. Built binaries are in `build/turret/` and `build/glove/`.

## Peripheral diagnostics

Serial command `i` scans the main board I2C bus, reports servo PWM frequency/attachment and wheel PWM duty, and shows raw PIR level and warmup status. Zero wheel frequency while duty is zero is expected with this Arduino core.

Serial command `t` disarms the wheels, keeps the laser off, cycles RGB red/green/blue, displays HARDWARE TEST, pulses the active buzzer for 150ms, and sweeps each servo through 80°, 100°, and 90°. It ends in hold mode. Ensure the mechanism can move through that small range. `s` aborts the sequence. Output devices need visual/audible confirmation; reported angles are commands, not feedback.

The latest run is saved in `device-test.log`. To repeat using the local Python environment, run `.venv/bin/python test_devices.py`. The glove and its MPU6050 are on the other ESP32 and cannot be checked through the main board when BLE is unavailable.

## Latest glove correction

The connected sensor responds at I2C 0x68 with chip ID 0x70 (MPU6500). Firmware now supports this device as well as MPU6050 through separate initialization paths. The corrected glove firmware was flashed and hash-verified; 100-sample calibration and live changing angle packets were observed. BLE is advertising; a main-board connection has not yet been confirmed. See GLOVE_VERIFICATION.md for current evidence.

WHEELS.md
# Four-wheel drive wiring and operation

This firmware now supports a **dual-channel L298N module with ENA, IN1, IN2, IN3, IN4, ENB pins**. This is a proposed hardware layout because your controller has not been identified. It is not universal firmware for arbitrary four-channel shields or I2C motor controllers. Check the labels before making these connections.

## Proposed wiring to the main ESP32

All turret connections in README.md remain assigned to their original GPIOs.

| L298N signal | Main ESP32 |
|---|---|
| IN1 | GPIO14 |
| IN2 | GPIO16 |
| IN3 | GPIO17 |
| IN4 | GPIO26 |
| ENA | GPIO2 |
| ENB | GPIO15 |
| GND | ESP32 GND and motor-supply negative |

**Remove both ENA and ENB jumper caps** before connecting the ESP32: the firmware controls those enables with PWM. Add a **10kΩ pull-down to GND on each ENA/ENB signal** so motors stay disabled during reset. GPIO2 and GPIO15 are ESP32 boot-strapping pins; do not let the module pull them up to 5V. This mapping is for the detected original ESP32; GPIO16/17 may be unavailable on boards with PSRAM.

Connect the two left motors in parallel to OUT1/OUT2 and the two right motors in parallel to OUT3/OUT4 **only if each channel can handle the combined stall current of its two motors**. The number of wheels alone does not establish driver suitability. Use another adequately rated driver if the combined load exceeds the module's continuous/thermal capability. Confirm each side rotates forward together; mirror-mounted motors may need opposite wire polarity.

Motor supply positive goes to the module's motor supply terminal, often labeled `12V`, `VS`, or `+Vm`. Choose the supply for the actual motor ratings and driver requirements. The terminal label does not mean every motor should receive 12V. The L298N module also needs its specified logic supply; its **5V regulator jumper is separate from ENA/ENB**. Configure it according to your particular module's documentation. Do not connect an external logic 5V source against an enabled onboard regulator output.

Keep the ESP32 on USB initially and the servos on their external regulated 5V supply. Share grounds. **Do not send motor/servo current through the breadboard rails or ESP32 power pins**: wire power directly with suitable wire and terminals. The breadboard can carry the logic connections and pull-down resistors. Keep supply wiring short and add suitable motor-noise suppression and supply decoupling. Keep the laser disconnected during initial drive testing.

## Controls

Open main-board Serial Monitor at **115200 baud**:

| Key | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `d` | Select wheel mode; freezes turret; requires neutral glove for 0.5 seconds to arm |
| `g` | Select turret gesture mode; wheels stop and disarm |
| `s` or `h` | Stop/disarm wheels and hold turret |
| `c` | Stop/disarm wheels and center turret |
| `l` | Existing one-second laser pulse, allowed only in turret gesture mode with live glove |
| `0` | Laser off |

In drive mode, pitch the glove forward to drive forward and backward to reverse. Roll right to turn right, left to turn left. Roll with neutral pitch to turn in place. Return to neutral to stop. If tilt is reversed for the way you mount your glove sensor, change the sign of the throttle expression in `WheelDrive.h`.

Mode selection currently uses USB serial because the diagram includes no mode button. The glove firmware already sends the angles required; it needs no update for wheel control. It must be flashed onto the second ESP32 and powered before drive mode can arm.

Wheels start disabled after every boot. Loss of fresh glove data stops and disarms them. A separate FreeRTOS task disables both enables if the main loop stops updating wheel commands for more than 250ms, even during a blocking BLE operation. Stale glove data is rejected after 300ms; return to neutral for 0.5 seconds before movement resumes. This software timeout coasts the motors; it does not provide mechanical braking or a physical emergency stop.

Initial duty is capped at **120/255**. This limits PWM duty, not measured speed or current. Some motors may not start at low duty. Adjust `MAX_PWM` only after testing the drivetrain with the wheels lifted. `INVERT_LEFT` and `INVERT_RIGHT` reverse the corresponding side without rewiring. The turret-mounted ultrasonic/PIR sensors remain advisory indicators; they do not provide collision avoidance for wheel movement.

## First test

1. Connect only the ESP32 logic and L298N, following the table and pull-down requirements. Raise the wheels off the surface before applying motor power.
2. Confirm the serial log says `Wheel PWM ready (L298N); wheels disarmed`.
3. Power the flashed glove, hold it flat, and wait for `link=1`.
4. Send `d`; hold neutral until `armed=1`, then apply a small pitch and check both sides.
5. Send `s` and confirm the wheels stop. Test loss of glove power and direction reversal before putting the chassis on the floor.

Implementation uses the [Espressif LEDC API](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/arduino-esp32/en/latest/api/ledc.html) and the L298's separate enable/direction inputs described by [STMicroelectronics](https://www.st.com/en/motor-drivers/l298.html).

## Bounded wheel diagnostic

The latest source adds `u` for a left-side forward pulse and `v` for a right-side forward pulse. Each is capped at PWM 80/255 and 200ms, with expiry enforced by the wheel-output task independently of the main loop. Both commands disarm gesture driving, freeze the turret and turn the laser off. `s` cancels a pulse. These commands are installed on the board. The first upload attempt was blocked by boot mode 0xB; the subsequent attempt succeeded and the flash hash was verified. Both enables were confirmed at duty 0 after startup. A subsequent pulse test confirmed the left and right PWM outputs individually at 5000Hz and duty80, followed by final duty0/0. Physical motor rotation requires user observation; see wheel-test.log.

If the controller wiring prevents flashing, power off the motor supply and disconnect the GPIO2-to-ENA signal while uploading. Ensure ENA/ENB jumper caps are removed and the intended pull-downs are installed before reconnecting. GPIO2 must be low or floating at reset to enter download mode; do not connect it to a module's 5V jumper pin.

## Extended diagnostic pending upload

The latest source adds uppercase U/V/J/K for left forward/right forward/left reverse/right reverse, each capped at 180/255 duty and 1500ms with task-enforced expiry. Lowercase u/v retain the 80/255, 200ms test. Command p reports direction levels and PWM duty. test_wheels_extended.py checks two active snapshots per phase, stops after unexpected output, and checks that both enables return to zero after expiry. Host tests and the full ESP32 build passed. Upload of this extended version failed with boot mode 0xB after the controller was reconnected; it is NOT yet installed. The old bounded-test firmware remains on the board.
